topic: Due dates for todos, with overdue items shown in red
rationale: Two runs. A read run first maps where todos are stored, rendered and tested, so the build run starts from facts instead of guesses. The build run then adds an optional due date to the model, the form and the list, marks overdue items and covers both with tests. One perspective each is enough; the change is small and well bounded.

clarifications.question: Should a due date include a time, or only a day?
clarifications.why: A time needs a time zone decision and a different input; a day does not.

runs.title: Map how todos are stored, rendered and tested
acceptance: The map names the file and function that stores a todo
The map names where the list is rendered and how tests are run
runs.prompt:
# Task
Find where todos are defined, stored, rendered and tested in this repo. Write the findings to docs/due-dates-map.md: file paths, function names, the test command and anything that would make adding a due date risky.

# Output
Only docs/due-dates-map.md. Change nothing else.

runs.title: Add an optional due date and mark overdue todos
acceptance: A todo can be saved with and without a due date
A todo whose due date is before today is shown in red
Tests cover both cases and pass
runs.prompt:
# Task
Read docs/due-dates-map.md first. Add an optional due date (day only) to the todo model, the add form and the list. Mark todos whose due date is before today in red. Add tests for saving with and without a date and for the overdue marker.

# Scope limit
Only the todo model, form, list and their tests. No restyling, no new dependencies.

# Not fixed
If you notice unrelated defects, list them under 'Not fixed' in docs/due-dates-report.md instead of changing them.

# Report
Write docs/due-dates-report.md: what changed, how to try it, the test output.
